Proposal for a Working Group to Define a Network ID 
Summary 
This document defines a proposal for a working group to develop a standard for identifiers for 
networks and associated health plans. 
 
Purpose 
This working group will define an identification scheme for networks and associated plans for 
use in Transparency in Coverage files, with the longer-term goal of creating public identifiers 
that facilitate consumersâ€™ use of price and coverage information in healthcare shopping. The 
identifier would be modeled on similar standards for VINs (ISO 3779:2009 and/or 49 CFR Part 
565 Subpart B) and credit card numbers (ISO/IEC 7812-1:2017).  
 
Problem 
Lack of clear identification of networks and associated health plans impedes many healthcare 
use cases, from accurate price transparency to health plan shopping to provider directory use. 
Absent a well-defined standard, insurers publishing TIC files and related data about provider-
network relationships such as provider directory websites and APIs, will continue to use 
fragmented and ad-hoc identifiers. 
 
Issues to be Addressed: 
 
- 
There is no single clear identifier for each insurer that aligns the issuer of each health 
plan with that planâ€™s network. 
o There is misalignment between current identifiers such as HIOS issuer IDs and 
the insurer or network management legal entity to which the provider 
organization is contractually bound 
o This creates ambiguity and duplication in price transparency data, reducing the 
quality and utility of this data. 
o The identity of the insurer (and plan or network) may also be out of alignment 
with provider directory endpoints and websites. 
 
 
  
- 
Insurers may have disparate and non-aligned definitions of products, networks, and 
plans. 
o This lack of alignment occurs both between different insurers as well as between 
different functional groups within insurers. 
o For example, sometimes a network is defined as a bag of provider contracts from 
which employer clients can choose in-network providers for their group. Other 
times the network may be defined as the final list of providers available to that 
group. 
- 
Identity of the network year-on-year is unclear and not aligned to plan definitions 
o There is no clear public standard for how networks evolve over time, and when 
changes to a network constitute a new network as opposed to providers 
entering and exiting an existing network. 
o There is also no clarity on the alignment of a planâ€™s term (i.e. the â€œplan yearâ€) 
with the identity of the network which the plan uses. Currently, QHP JSON files 
indicating network participation use â€œplan yearâ€. This is mostly sufficient for 
QHPs, since all of these plans have a plan year which follows the calendar year.  
For plans whose term does not follow the calendar year, the alignment of the 
network with the plan is unclear. 
 
The working group would review this list of issues, identify and additions or changes, and create 
an Agile-style backlog of issues that need to be addressed. â€œReleasesâ€ of the network 
identification standard would occur when the group determined that sufficient progress had 
been made on key issues to make the scheme usable. 
 
Proposed Network Identification Scheme 
Structure of the identifier 
A standard identifier for health insurance networks and associated plans should adopt 
structuring principles similar to the automotive Vehicle Identification Number (ISO 3779) and 
credit card Primary Account Number  (ISO 7812). The VIN standard uses three distinct 
segments: a World Manufacturer Identifier (WMI) that identifies the manufacturer, a Vehicle 
Descriptor Section (VDS), and Vehicle Indicator Section (VIS). Similarly, the credit card Primary 
Account Number (PAN) consists of an Issuer Identification Number (IIN), and an Account 
Identifier. 
 
  
A standard for identifying networks should similarly involve an identifier for the insurer, akin to 
the WMI or IIN. Establishing the public identity of the insurer likely requires some work to 
create uniformity (see question 5 in Frequently Asked Questions for further details). Having a 
well-established public identity for each insurer will be profoundly useful in work such as FHIR 
Brands, the National Provider Directory, FHIR Provider Directory APIs, and many other 
interoperability and consumer information exchange use cases. 
The network itself should be identified underneath the insurer, similar to the way the Vehicle 
Descriptor Section of a VIN falls under the World Manufacturer Identifier. This may require 
addressing some complexities such as cross-contracted/shared networks like BlueCard, 
reciprocity agreements for care outside of planâ€™s service area, and networks created and 
managed by entities that do not themselves offer insurance plans. 
 
Requirements for the Identifier 
- 
The identifier must permit resolution of the insurer or network management entity that 
creates or operates the network. 
- 
There must be a mapping from health plans to the networks they leverage that enables 
unambiguous linkage of contractual rates published in TIC files to plan design data and 
coverage rules. 
- 
The structure of the identification must permit unambiguous representation of 
negotiated rates, as well as other relevant contractual terms that affect the price a 
consumer will pay for a specific medical service from a specific provider. 
- 
The identification scheme should eliminate or minimize duplicated representation of 
any single contractually defined negotiation rate within Transparency in Coverage (TIC) 
files. 
- 
The identification scheme should permit resolving â€œcustomizationâ€ of networks through 
addition or removal of providers, or superseding contracts which override the price 
defined in the â€œbase networkâ€ contract. Our current proposed solution would be to 
enable identification of â€œbase networksâ€ and â€œdeltasâ€ from that to minimize duplication; 
the working group would vet and improve such a scheme. 
 
See question 6 in the FAQ about a network ID for an example of the â€œbase + deltaâ€ structure. 
 
 
  
Participants 
Potential participants include 
- 
Insurers 
o Provider network management teams 
o Provider directory teams or vendors 
o Teams or vendors preparing or hosting TIC files 
- 
TIC Data Users 
o Vendors such as Turquoise Health, Serif Health and others 
o Researchers who use this data 
- 
Patient and Consumer Organizations 
- 
CMS and/or state insurance regulators 
- 
Other interoperability stakeholders

# Comment Analysis Template: CMS-2026-1255-0001

## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Not separately identified in extracted text; proposal attached to Consumers' Checkbook/Center for the Study of Services submission.
- **Stakeholder type:** Advocacy Group / Consumer organization / Technical standards stakeholder
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** Demonstrates expertise in Transparency in Coverage files, provider directories, FHIR Brands, National Provider Directory concepts, and FHIR Provider Directory APIs.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The attachment proposes a working group to define standardized identifiers for health insurance networks and associated plans. Although it does not directly address drug prior authorization, it supports broader CMS interoperability and transparency goals by seeking consistent identifiers that link TIC rates, plan design data, coverage rules, provider directories, and consumer shopping tools.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** GENERAL; API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING and FHIR-IG-REQUIRED indirectly through references to provider directory APIs and standards-based public identifiers.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** 49 CFR Part 565 Subpart B; ISO 3779:2009; ISO/IEC 7812-1:2017. No CMS-2026-1255 CFR provisions cited.
- **Standards referenced:** VIN standard ISO 3779; credit card PAN/IIN standard ISO/IEC 7812-1; FHIR Brands; National Provider Directory; FHIR Provider Directory APIs; QHP JSON files.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Working Group for Network and Plan Identifiers**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Fragmented, ad hoc identifiers impede price transparency, health plan shopping, provider directory use, and consumer use of coverage information.
- **Specific request:** Convene a working group to define an identification scheme for networks and associated plans.

**Topic 2: Identifier Requirements and Structure**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Clarify / Modify
- **Rationale:** A useful identifier must resolve the insurer or network management entity, map plans to networks, represent negotiated rates and relevant contractual terms, reduce duplication, and support customized employer-plan networks.
- **Specific request:** Model the identifier on segmented structures like VINs and credit card PANs, with insurer and network components and support for base-network-plus-delta customization.

**Topic 3: Alignment with Interoperability Assets**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; GENERAL
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** A public insurer identity would be useful for FHIR Brands, the National Provider Directory, FHIR Provider Directory APIs, and other consumer information exchange use cases.
- **Specific request:** Ensure the network identifier can support provider directory websites/APIs and other interoperability tools.

**Topic 4: Stakeholder Participation and Standards Process**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Identifier rules must reflect insurer operations, TIC production, data-user needs, consumer perspectives, and regulatory oversight.
- **Specific request:** Include insurers, provider directory teams/vendors, TIC file teams/vendors, TIC data users, researchers, patient/consumer organizations, CMS, state regulators, and other interoperability stakeholders.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

No CMS-0062-P numbered solicitation is directly answered. The attachment is most relevant to general RFI solicitations (S66-S82) related to interoperability, public data infrastructure, and consumer-facing transparency, and indirectly to FHIR-IG-REQUIRED topics concerning standards development and adoption.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Establish a working group to define a standard identifier for networks and associated plans.
2. Create a public insurer identifier segment and subordinate network identifier segment.
3. Map health plans unambiguously to the networks they use.
4. Support representation of negotiated rates, contractual terms, and plan coverage rules.
5. Minimize duplicated rate representation in TIC files.
6. Include base-network and delta structures for customized employer plans.
7. Include insurers, vendors, TIC data users, researchers, consumer groups, CMS, and state regulators in the working group.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** No single clear insurer identifier; inconsistent definitions of products, networks, and plans; unclear year-to-year network identity; misalignment between plan years and network identity.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Ambiguity and duplication in price transparency data; reduced utility for provider directories, health plan shopping, and consumer-facing coverage information.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Complex network structures, shared networks, reciprocity arrangements, non-insurer network managers, employer customizations, and plan terms that do not align with calendar years.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** None.
- **Studies or research referenced:** ISO 3779:2009, 49 CFR Part 565 Subpart B, and ISO/IEC 7812-1:2017 as analogous identifier schemes.
- **Examples provided:** HIOS issuer ID misalignment; different definitions of networks as contract sets versus final provider lists; QHP JSON plan-year limitations; base networks and deltas for employer customizations.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Consumers, insurers, providers, provider-directory vendors, TIC vendors, TIC data users, researchers, CMS, state regulators, and interoperability stakeholders.
- **Economic implications:** Could improve the value of TIC files and reduce duplication and ambiguity in rate data production and reuse.
- **Technical feasibility:** Feasible through an Agile-style standards working group and staged releases, but requires resolving complex data-model and governance questions.
- **Patient care impact:** Indirect; better network and coverage information can help consumers identify relevant prices, coverage rules, and in-network providers.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive of additional standardization
- **Tone:** Technical and constructive
- **Priority level:** Medium

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "Lack of clear identification of networks and associated health plans impedes many healthcare use cases." - Context: Problem statement for the working group.
2. "A standard for identifying networks should similarly involve an identifier for the insurer." - Context: Proposed segmented identifier structure.
3. "There must be a mapping from health plans to the networks they leverage." - Context: Identifier requirement for linking rates, plan designs, and coverage rules.
4. "Potential participants include Insurers... TIC Data Users... Patient and Consumer Organizations... CMS and/or state insurance regulators." - Context: Proposed stakeholder composition.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - The proposal aims to make price and coverage information more usable for consumers.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - It lays out identifier requirements, structures, and staged working-group releases.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - The comment proposes development of a new standard modeled on mature identifier schemes.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - The working group depends on broad participation across insurers, vendors, consumers, regulators, and data users.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - Accurate network and plan identification can support healthcare shopping and provider selection.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - The proposal is designed for TIC files, provider directories, QHP JSON files, and plan/network relationships.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - Provider directory vendors, TIC vendors, and data users are explicit participants and beneficiaries.
